guardians could be responsible for up to 50 minors and were reported to lack sufficient capacity or expertise.","notes":["The excerpt supports the listed services but does not expressly characterize legal representation or youth-care services as limited."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0011-R03-E010","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0011-R03-E011","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0011-R03-E012","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0011-R03-E013","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0011-R03-E014","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0011-R03-E015","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"NGOs criticized the Afghan admission programme in 2023 for slow implementation, opaque or insufficiently transparent selection, restrictive agency-based nomination and IT procedures, inadequate staffing, passport barriers, and failure to meet the originally envisaged 1,000 admissions per month.","notes":["The excerpt reports that NGOs demanded fulfillment of the originally envisaged 1,000 admissions per month; it does not independently quantify or explicitly state that the target had already failed."]}]}
